checks.criterion: No implementation code present (no .ex code bodies, signatures/types only)
checks.evidence: grep for 'def ', 'case ... do', 'with ... do' inside the doc found none -- the only 'end' tokens (lines 121, 124) close the §2 module-layout skeleton, which contains a comment placeholder ('# export/2, import/3, and their private pipeline helpers') with no real body. The ExportDocument defstruct/@enforce_keys/@type block (§4.1) is a struct type-shape declaration, not a function body -- this exact pattern (defstruct + @enforce_keys + @type t inside a design doc) is the established project convention, confirmed present in lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex's own shipped Node/Edge/Violation struct defs (lines 79-101, 118-119) that this design explicitly cites as its precedent. Pipeline steps (E0/E1, I0/I1/I2) are prose + illustrative map/struct literals describing what gets built, not compilable function bodies.

checks.criterion: The imported_by parameter (not literally named in REQ-034's text) is explicitly reasoned/flagged rather than silently invented
checks.evidence: §4.3 explicitly states 'imported_by is this design's own addition -- not named anywhere in REQ-034's text' and justifies it: create/2's create_attrs() type requires required(:created_by) => Ecto.UUID.t() -- independently re-confirmed directly against lib/letflow/definitions.ex lines 115-122, this requirement is real, not fabricated. ExportDocument (§4.1, REQ-034's own enumerated 7-field list) carries no creator-identity field, so import/3 has no other source for the required key. OQ-3 (§8) further flags the open question of who supplies imported_by at the eventual call site. This is genuine reasoning traced to a real, re-verified shipped-code constraint, not an invented parameter.
